next_steps.title: 1. Measure whole-PR selection benefit
next_steps.action: Replay complete historical App-only PR base/head pairs plus Gateway/Controller positive controls through the actual production selector, then execute matched required-check arms for a representative change.
next_steps.acceptance: Count complete required feedback, action CPU and failures. Selected-test reductions alone do not qualify this branch; App Pod may still dominate the critical path.

next_steps.title: 2. Remove deployment machinery from protocol contracts
next_steps.action: Audit which App Pod/central cases require Kubernetes reconciliation, issuance, workload identity, volume replacement or actual suspension. Run pure Session, History, authorization and turn-state contracts against real service processes with a small database fixture; keep real deployment witnesses for every unique boundary. Spike the largest transferable critical-path group first.
next_steps.acceptance: Proceed only with an assertion-to-owner inventory, a real failing regression control, and an end-to-end saving plausibly ≥30%. No blanket path filter and no fake replacement for a real deployment assertion.

next_steps.title: 3. Qualify a promising architecture
next_steps.action: If the small screen clears the latency/compute threshold, run 30 matched PR pairs and ≥100 fresh contract executions across three busy windows, warm/cold conditions and a four-PR burst. Include seeded/historical failures and scenario-isolation controls.
next_steps.acceptance: ≥30% faster complete required feedback; CPU ratio ≤1.25; no lost unique assertion or unexplained failure signature. Record p90, reruns, source/image inputs and unknown metrics.
